overview: White develops the queen's bishop to g5 at once, a Trompowsky-style pin idea against 1...d5, before playing e3 and Nf3. Black often asks the bishop a question with ...h6 and ...c6 or plays ...f6 or ...Nf6 and ...Ne4. White's aim is a comfortable development with the bishop outside the pawn chain and a flexible pawn centre; there is little theory.

white_ideas.idea: Bg5 then e3, Nf3, Bd3 and c3, a Torre or Colle-like set-up
Pin or harass Black's kingside, pushing Bh4 or Bxf6 when useful
Keep the pawn centre flexible with a later c4 or e4

black_ideas.idea: ...h6 and ...c6 to put the question and then play ...Bf5 and ...e6
...f6 or ...Nf6-e4 to challenge the bishop and take space
Build a normal Slav or QGD set-up without weaknesses

typical_structures.structure: d4/e3 against d5/e6 or c6, flexible centre like a Torre or London

character.notes: Quiet development with no forcing play; 2...Nf6 or ...f6 can bring some sharpness but main line is a calm game.

gambit.notes: No material is given in the main lines.

soundness.notes: Sound, a legitimate if unambitious White try.

structure.notes: Pawn centre in tension, nothing committed, like a Torre or London.

approach.notes: Less common than 2.Bf4, used as a side line by some strong players but not a main choice.

level.notes: Few moves to memorise but understanding of the Bg5 placement is helpful.

sublines_that_differ.name: Hodgson Attack 2...f6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black weakens the kingside but takes space; unusual, tricky play.

character.reason: Quiet development without forcing tactics or especially solid walls.

structure.reason: Centre left in tension, like a Torre or London.

approach.reason: Less common but played by strong players, so not offbeat.

level.reason: Simple development with some subtlety in bishop placement.

plans.reason: No clear plan from the closed list fits a position this undeveloped.
